attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 10, using pg_basebackup with physical replication slots and a replicator role (password generated on-node and relayed node-to-node via cluster SSH keys, never exposed in the final report). Simulated primary loss by stopping PostgreSQL on node1, confirmed both standbys were fully caught up (no data-loss risk), promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote, repointed node3 to stream from node2, then rebuilt node1 from a fresh base backup of node2 and brought it back online as a standby. Verified zero committed-data loss throughout (all pre-failover rows plus new writes present on every node). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node3, node1, then node2/the primary last) using systemd reboot, proving each node's changed boot_id and confirming PostgreSQL, recovery state, and streaming replication/slots fully recovered after each restart, with a final cross-node row-count consistency check (5/5/5) after all restarts completed.
